newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Essex Refinery Corp wins Kazakh oil refinery stake.
newsitem.headline: Essex Refinery Corp wins Kazakh oil refinery stake.

text.p: Essex Refinery Corp, registered in the British Virgin Islands, has won a tender for a 53.1 percent stake in Kazakhstan's Atyrau oil refinery, a senior Kazakh privatisation official said on Monday.

"Their (Essex Refinery Corp) conditions and investment plan were far better than those of the other competitors," said the official with Kazakhstan's State Privatisation Committee. He added Essex would invest over $1 billion in the refinery, which has an annual capacity of 4.5 million tonnes.

The official said Essex had also won ownership of a power station providing Kazakhstan's western Atyrau region with electricity. The facility operates at only 150 megawatts of its 220 megawatt capacity.
Unsuccessful bidders in the refinery tender were Geneva-based companies, Lia Oil SA and Petroleum Ltd.
The committee official said Essex would invest $105 million over the period 1997-1999, another $260 million by 2004 and a further $650 million by 2005.
Essex would also provide $30-35 million in working capital this year and agreed to earmark 10-15 percent of net profit to social and environmental projects.
One of three oil refineries in the resource-rich republic, Atyrau is the only one that runs on Kazakh feedstock, sourced from the Emba and Mangistau oil fields in western Kazakhstan.
